result:
This diff is small, but it bundles three separate controlled items — a wording change, an autonomous financial capability, and a public safety claim — and the interesting risk is in how they interact, not in any one line. "Smoke test and merge" would verify the tool runs, not that these stay in sync later.

| Item | Type | Current state | Intended state | Why controlled | Evidence / gap | Owner | Re-check trigger |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Support-bot system prompt | Prompt | Existing wording | "More proactive" wording | Behavior/trust — proactive wording combined with new refund power could push the bot toward offering refunds unprompted | PR diff (link it) | Prompt owner | Any further prompt edit; observed pattern of bot volunteering refunds |
| `issue_refund(amount, order_id)` tool | Tool / agent power grant | No autonomous refund capability | Bot can approve refunds up to $50 with no human sign-off | Direct increase in agent power over money, no human in the loop — highest-stakes item in this PR | Gap: no risk assessment, no abuse/fraud monitoring spec, no audit log of autonomous approvals found in the diff | Eng lead + a finance/risk owner (not just eng) | Any change to the $ threshold; refund-rate anomaly; any incident; removal/weakening of monitoring |
| Help-center article on refund review | Public doc / claim | States "A human always reviews refunds before they are issued." | Sentence deleted | Public claim about how the system works — must match actual behavior or you're misrepresenting the process to customers | PR diff | Docs/support content owner | Any further change to refund process; any other doc/ToS/marketing page still claiming human review (contradiction) |
| Consistency between claim #2 and #3 | Cross-cutting check | Doc will say nothing about auto-approval | Doc should ideally state accurately that refunds under $50 may be auto-approved, not just delete the old sentence | Silent deletion can leave customers with a false impression by omission rather than an accurate one | Gap — this isn't addressed by the PR as described | Docs owner + eng lead jointly | Any future refund-threshold change (doc must move with it) |

Two things worth flagging before merge:

- The tool grant and the doc edit are coupled — if one changes later without the other, you get a public claim that's wrong. That coupling itself needs an owner, not just the two items separately.
- "Quick smoke test" covers the tool works, not that a $50 autonomous refund limit is the right number, that abuse patterns are monitored, or that the new doc wording is accurate rather than just quieter. Those need a sign-off from whoever owns refund/financial risk, not just eng review.

Want me to draft this as an actual `controlled-items.md` you can attach to the PR?
